title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: arXiv:2610.30006v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI-generated text detectors are increasingly deployed in consequential settings---peer review, education, admissions, journalism, and content moderation---where their outputs directly affect individuals. Yet the strongest detectors are fine-tuned neural classifiers whose decisions are opaque, while transparent alternatives (stylometric and linguistic-feature classifiers) underperform them by wide margins. We present a pipeline that converts a fine-tuned neural detector into a classifier that operates on human-readable concepts. We accomplish this by training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) directly on a detector's residual stream, assigning auto-interpretation labels to each SAE feature, and retaining only features whose generated descriptions pass a global fidelity threshold. translated_title: 基于稀疏自编码器构建可审计的AI文本检测器
translated_abstract: AI生成的文本检测器正越来越多地被部署在具有重大影响的场景中——如同行评审、教育、招生、新闻和内容审核——在这些场景中，检测器的输出会直接影响个人。然而，性能最强的检测器是经过微调的神经网络分类器，其决策过程是不透明的，而透明的替代方案（如文体计量和语言特征分类器）的性能则远远落后。我们提出了一种流水线，能够将微调的神经检测器转换为基于人类可读概念运行的分类器。我们的实现方式是：直接在检测器的残差流上训练稀疏自编码器（SAEs），为每个SAE特征分配自动解释标签，并仅保留那些生成的描述能通过全局保真度阈值的特征。随后，我们仅在这些可解释的特征上训练一个轻量级分类器。我们发现，我们的SAE能够恢复出与高度具体且具有预测性的（摘要在此处截断）潜在概念相对应的特征。
tldr: 该论文提出一种流水线，通过在神经检测器的残差流上训练稀疏自编码器、自动生成特征解释标签并按全局保真度阈值筛选特征，从而将不透明的AI文本检测器转化为基于人类可读概念运行的可审计分类器。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a pipeline that converts an opaque fine-tuned neural AI-text detector into an auditable classifier operating on human-readable concepts by training sparse autoencoders on the detector's residual stream, auto-labeling features, and retaining only those passing a global fidelity threshold.
